newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE EXTEND UNBEATEN STREAK TO 11 GAMES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE EXTEND UNBEATEN STREAK TO 11 GAMES.

text.p: Peter Forsberg had two goals and two assists as the Colorado Avalanche tied a franchise record by extending their unbeaten streak to 11 games with a 4-1 defeat of the Detroit Red Wings on Wednesday.

Forsberg scored in each of the first two periods for Colorado, which was facing the Red Wings for the first time since eliminating them in the Western Conference finals. Forsberg's four points moved him into a tie with teammate Joe Sakic for the league lead with 30.
Sandis Ozolinsh added a pair of power-play tallies for the Avalanche.
The Avalanche improved to 9-0-2 in their last 11 games, matching the mark set as the Quebec Nordiques in March 1981.

"We were real good," Avalanche coach Marc Crawford said. "We had a few breakdowns, we're going to have a few every game. But whenever they started getting momentum going, we throttled it. The whole group in there was focused and played with some passion tonight."
Patrick Roy stopped 21 shots, 11 in the third period, for Colorado. Roy is 8-0-1 in his last nine starts and leads the league with 12 victories.
"We were solid offensively and defensively," Roy said. "That's how we've been playing for a while now."
Steve Yzerman scored the only goal for Detroit, which lost for just the third time in its last 13 games.
"They played very solid," Red Wings coach Scotty Bowman said. "They weren't weak in many areas."
In Montreal, Ray Sheppard scored twice and added an assist as the Florida Panthers held on for a 5-3 victory over the sputtering Canadiens.
Sheppard's power-play tally capped a three-goal first period and he scored again with 58 seconds to go in the third period after Montreal climbed within 4-3.

Bill Lindsay added a goal and an assist and John Vanbiesbrouck made 18 saves after missing one game with a thigh bruise as the Panthers improved the league's best record to 11-2-4. Florida also is an NHL-best 5-1-3 on the road.
Mark Recchi and Saku Koivu each had a goal and an assist for the Canadiens.
In Ottawa, Curtis Joseph stopped 28 shots for his third shutout of the season and added an assist as the Edmonton Oilers blanked the slumping Senators 4-0.
Joseph stopped 14 shots in the first period, six in the second and eight in the third for his eighth career shutout and second in six days.

Todd Marchant, Mariusz Czerkawski, Ryan Smyth and Miroslav Satan scored the goals. Marchant missed a penalty shot off the right goal post with 88 seconds left in the game after he was tripped by Steve Duchesne on a breakaway.
Joseph got his assist when his clearing pass got Marchant going on a partial breakaway for a goal in the first period.
In Anaheim, Jari Kurri scored with 9:08 left in the third period as the Mighty Ducks edged the Toronto Maple Leafs 3-2 for their first-ever win against goaltender Felix Potvin.
Potvin is now 5-1-2 lifetime against the Mighty Ducks. The Maple Leafs lost for the third time in four games.
Anaheim star Paul Kariya, who missed the first 12 games with an abdominal injury, suffered a slight concussion late in the first period and did not return.
Mats Sundin scored twice for Toronto with Doug Gilmour assisting on both goals.
In New York, Pat Falloon's power-play goal 5:51 into the third period lifted the Philadelphia Flyers to a 2-1 win over the slumping Rangers.
The Flyers won for just the third time in their last 19 visits to Madison Square Garden (3-13-3). The Rangers are winless in their last five games (0-4-1).
Shjon Podein scored Philadelphia's first goal. Brian Leetch tied it up for New York in the second period.
Mike Richter made 35 saves for New York, but suffered his third straight loss. Ron Hextall stopped 26 shots.
In Uniondale, New York, Bryan McCabe put a wrist shot through Corey Hirsch's pads 45 seconds into overtime, giving the Islanders a 5-4 victory over the Vancouver Canucks.
Derek King and linemate Zigmund Palffy each had a goal and two assists for the Islanders, who broke a 10-game winless streak in overtime (0-3-7).
In Dallas, Dwayne Roloson made 35 saves in his NHL debut and Theoren Fleury scored with 9:21 left in the third period as the Calgary Flames rallied for a 3-3 tie against the Stars.
Roloson, 27, allowed three goals in the first period, but stopped 10 shots in the second, six in the third and four in overtime as the Flames ended a four-game losing streak.
Jarome Iginla and Robert Reichel also scored for Calgary. Sergei Zubov, Greg Adams and Pat Verbeek tallied for Dallas.
